messages.subject: TimeSeries align odd behavior
messages.subject_clean: TimeSeries align odd behavior
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rmetrics-core team,
I have a question about a strange behavior of timeSeries align function.

For example, consider the following timeSeries:
> TS <- timeSeries(c(1,NA,3,4),
                   charvec=c('2010-01-01','2010-01-02','2010-01-03','2010-01-05'),
                   format='%Y-%m-%d', zone='GMT', units='V')

> TS
GMT
            V
2010-01-01  1
2010-01-02 NA
2010-01-03  3
2010-01-05  4

If we call the function align, with method='fillNA':
> align(TS,by='day',include.weekends=T,method='fillNA')
we get the following result:
> GMT
            V
2010-01-01  1
2010-01-02  2
2010-01-03  3
2010-01-04 NA
2010-01-05  4

So, basically the NA in the original timeSeries is interpolated and then the missing day is correctly added by setting the value to NA.
That doesn't seem correct to me, since only the missing days of the timeSeries should be filled with NA, while the other values should remain unchanged (in particular in case of fillNA method).

Looking at the code, it appears clear what happens: when the method is fillNA, an approxfun with method "linear" is applied. Then to replace the interpolated values with NA the following code is performed:
if (Method == "fillNA")
      yout[!(xout %in% u)] = NA
but obviously this code will put NA only in the missing dates added to the original ts and not to ALL the interpolated values.

Is this the desired behavior?
If so, in my opinion should be clearly specified in the align documentation.


Thanks in advance for any answer and thanks a lot for your work on this great package.

Regards,
Marco Giuliano

Fax. +39 0173 620299 / +39 0173 433111
Web Site www.ors.it

messages.subject: stabledist
messages.subject_clean: stabledist
messages.body_plain:
Dear Oliver
(I'm writing in English because of the CC).


On Mon, Oct 29, 2012 at 12:20 PM, Kley, Oliver <oliver.kley at tum.de> wrote:
> Lieber Herr Maechler,
>
> ich wollte das stabledist package von rmetrics installieren, wie im wiki beschrieben:
>
>
> The script installs all Rmetrics packages from your default CRAN repository ('repos'). This will ensure that all packages are up-to-date.
>
> Open an R process and type the following :
>
>    source("http://www.rmetrics.org/Rmetrics.R")
>    install.Rmetrics()
>
>
> allerdings, neben der installation zahlreicher pakete, kam insbesondere die folgende meldung, in deren vorletzter zeile steht, dass stabledist nicht verfuegbar ist --koennen Sie mir weiterhelfen?
>
>
>
> + source("http://www.rmetrics.org/Rmetrics.R")
> +    install.Rmetrics()
> Warning in install.packages(pkgs = pkgs, ...) :
>   argument 'lib' is missing: using '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library'
> Warning in install.packages(pkgs = pkgs, ...) :
>   'lib = "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"' is not writable
> --- Please select a CRAN mirror for use in this session ---
> Loading Tcl/Tk interface ... done
> Warning: dependency ?stabledist? is not available
> also installing the dependencies ?numDeriv?, ?DistributionUtils?, ?GeneralizedHyperbolic?

Yes, indeed this is a bug in the  install.Rmetrics() function;
Unfortunately, even though I'm part of Rmetrics-core,
I have no write access to  http://www.rmetrics.org/Rmetrics.R
which defines the  install.Rmetrics() function  and so I cannot fix it.

HOWEVER, there is an easy workaround:
do

install.packages("stabledist")

before doing the other installations.

Please let me know if you have problems, observe pecularities, ... in package
'stabledist'.

Best regards,
Martin M?chler


>
> Viele Gruesse
>
> Oliver Kley
>
